# Configure IBM Verify for agentic IAM

@include 'alerts/enterprise-and-hcp.mdx'

Configure users and OIDC applications in IBM Verify to use with Vault Enterprise
agentic IAM.


## Before you start

- **You must have an IBM Verify tenant**. If you do not have a tenant, you can
  [sign up for a free trial](https://docs.verify.ibm.com/verify/docs/getting-started-signing-up-for-a-free-trial)
  to evaluate the integration process.

- **You must have the [`oauth2c`](https://github.com/SecureAuthCorp/oauth2c) CLI**.
  You need `oauth2c` installed and in your system `PATH` to interact with OAuth
  2.0 authorization servers.

- **You must have [`curl`](https://curl.se/)** or some other tool to make API
  calls.

- **You must have [`jq`](https://jqlang.org/) installed** to use the example
  commands as written.


## Step 1: Create users in Verify

You need to create accounts for the human user and agent user in Verify and note
their user IDs.

1. Access your Verify tenant as an admin user.

1. Create and configure a user account for the human user that will use the AI
   agent or application.

    1. Click **Directory** in the navigation menu.
    1. Click **Users & groups**.
    1. Click **Add user**.
    1. Select an identity provider, such as **IBMid** or your preferred provider.
    1. In the **User name** field, enter a username value.
    1. In the **Preferred e-mail** field, enter a valid email address.
    1. Click **Save**.

1. Find and note the user ID:

    1. Click **Directory**.
    1. Click **Users & groups**.
    1. For the user you just created, click the **User details** icon.
    1. The user ID appears on the user profile page. You need this user ID value to
      later configure the external ID in the Vault entity alias.

  ![Get user ID value](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-verify-app000.png)

1. Repeat the process to create a user account for the agent or other AI
   application that will act on behalf of a human user and note the agent user
   ID.


## Step 2: Create an OIDC application in Verify

Configure a
[public or a confidential client](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.1)
OIDC application that issues JWT access tokens for the user and the agent or AI
application that performs operations on behalf of the user.

1. Access your Verify tenant as an admin user.

1. In the navigation menu, click **Applications** → **Applications**.

1. Click **Add an application**.

1. For application type, click **OpenID Connect**.

   ![Choose OpenID Connect application type](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-verify-app00.png)

1. Click **Add Application**.

1. Under **OpenID Connect** enter a name for the application. For example,
   `vault-authn-entry`.

1. Update the **Description** field as necessary.

1. For **Company name**, enter the required value.

1. Click **Add owner** to assign an admin user as the owner of this application.

1. Enter an admin username in the search field.

1. Click an admin user to highlight it.

1. Click **OK** to assign the admin user to this application.


## Step 3: Configure sign-on for the application

![Application sign-on settings](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-verify-app2.png)

1. Click **Sign-on** to configure the application sign on settings.

1. In the **Application URL** field, enter the main URL or home page of the app
   to add as the resource server. The application URL is the entry point of the
   user to interact with the application. You can configure the application URL
   to be appropriate for your AI application UI or chat interface.

1. Enable the necessary grant types. Browser driven flows use the Authorization
   code grant, and the resource server needs Client Credentials to
   authenticate with the authorization server to exchange the code for the security token.

   For **Grant types**, click and enable the following:

   - **Authorization code**.
   - **Client credentials**.
   - **Resource owner password credentials (ROPC)**

   <Warning>

   The ROPC grant is enabled just for demonstration of a script-driven
   on-behalf-of workflow in this documentation.
   **Do not enable ROPC in non-development environments**.

   </Warning>

1. For **Response types** click the response of the Authorization server when
  the user authenticates. Click the checkbox for **code** to use an Authz Code
  Grant flow.

2. For **Response modes** uncheck every mode except for **query**.

3. Ensure that **Public client (no client secret)** is unchecked to enforce
   a private client application.

   ![Application sign-on settings](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-verify-app3.png)

4. In the **Redirect URIs** field, enter a valid URI for the authorization
   server redirect to the URL containing the code as a query parameter.

5. Under **Token settings** > **Access token format**, select **JWT**.

6. Click the **Generate refresh token** checkbox.

   ![Application sign-on settings continued](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-verify-app4.png)

7. Click **Save** to save the application settings.

8. After saving the application, you arrive at the **Entitlements** tab where
   you must click the **Automatic access for all users and groups** radio
   button to enable access.

9. Click **Save** to save the application settings.

10. When prompted to update the workflow, click **OK**.


## Step 4: Configure an "on behalf of" relationship

Configure the on behalf of (OBO) relationship between the user/subject and the
agent or AI application. You must configure the `act` and `may_act` claims in
the configured OIDC application introspection endpoints.

1. Click **Applications** → **Applications**.

2. Click the gear icon next to your application name to open settings.

3. Click **Sign-on**.

4. Scroll down to **Client ID** and copy the value. Note and save the Client ID
   for configuring custom request rules later.

   ![Application Client ID](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-verify-app5.png)

5. Scroll down to **Endpoint configuration**.

6. Next to the **Introspect** settings, click the edit icon that resembles
   a pencil.

   ![Edit introspect settings](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-verify-app6.png)

7. Click the arrow next to **Add attribute**.

8. Click **Add custom rule**.

9. Within the **Request rule** text area, enter the following JSON which
   uses the client ID of the OIDC application. Paste the client ID value you
   just copied to replace the "CLIENT_ID" placeholder text.

   ```json
   {"client_id":"CLIENT_ID"}
   ```

10. Click **OK**.

11. Map the custom rule to the **Target attribute** `may_act`.

   ![Map the custom rule](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-verify-app7.png)

12. Click **OK**.

13. Scroll down to **Custom scopes and API access**.

14. Prevent the client from requesting unknown scopes by checking
   **Restrict custom scopes**.

15. Add `email` to a custom scope.

16. Add `openid` to a custom scope.

17. Add `profile` to a custom scope.

18. Click **Save**.

<Tip>

A well-known URL like `/.well-known/openid-configuration` provides a standardized
way for clients to automatically discover the metadata for an identity
provider, including supported scopes, public keys, and endpoint locations.
Using a well-known URL lets your application configure itself dynamically without
you having to hardcode every individual API URL.

Well known URLs for IBM Verify adhere to the following pattern:

```plaintext
https://TENANT_NAME.verify.ibm.com/oauth2/.well-known/openid-configuration
```

Note your well known URL for use later when you configure Vault.

</Tip>


## Step 5: Configure API client access

Configure a new API client for the IBM Verify tenant for API access:

1. In the navigation menu, click **Security**.

2. Click **Add API client**.

3. Click the checkbox for each client access entitlement that your agent or
   AI application use case requires.

4. Click **Next**.

5. The client ID gets automatically generated. Choose the client authentication
   method your use case requires or leave at **Default**.

6. Click **Next**.

7. Leave the custom scopes which the client can request unchanged unless your
   use case requires changing them.

8. Click **Next**.

9. Leave the IP filtering setting unchanged unless you need to filter the
   client API access by IP address or CIDR.

10. Click **Next**.

11. If your use case requires additional properties, enter their names and
   values. The screenshot show just an example value. Use your actual values.

12. click **Next**.

13. In the **Name** field, enter a machine friendly name like
   `hashicups-print-agent`. Add a description and any tags as well.

14. Click **Create API client**.

For more detailed configuration options, refer to the
[Verify API documenation](https://docs.verify.ibm.com/verify/page/api-documentation).


## Step 6: Create authorization detail type in Verify

You need to create an authorization details schema to define how information
gets structured, validated, and presented for consent during authentication
flows.

1. Click **Applications**.

2. Click **Authorization detail types**.

3. Click **Create**.

4. Under **General details**, select the **Custom** radio button.

5. In the **Name** field, define a name for this authorization detail type,
   enter the string `vault:path_access`.

6. In the **Description** field, enter a description for the type.

   ![Authorization type configuration](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-verify-app11.png)

7. In the **Schema** text area, paste the JSON schema defining the
   `authorization_details` query parameter:

   ```json
   {
     "type": "object",
     "required": [
       "type",
       "path",
       "capabilities"
     ],
     "additionalProperties": false,
     "properties": {
       "type": {
         "const": "vault:path_access"
       },
       "path": {
         "type": "string",
         "pattern": "^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$"
       },
       "capabilities": {
         "type": "array",
         "uniqueItems": true,
         "items": {
           "type": "string",
           "enum": [
             "read",
             "create",
             "update",
             "delete",
             "sudo",
             "list",
             "deny"
           ]
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```

8. Leave **Consent mapping** settings unchanged, and click **Next**.

9. For **Consent configuration** method, select **Inline HTML**.

10. For **Consent text**, enter `<div>EXAMPLE CONSENT TEXT</div>`.

11. Click **Create**.


## Step 7: Configure the secure token service client

Configure a security token service (STS) client for performing token exchange.
This STS client performs both the token exchange representing OBO semantics,
and the addition of an `authorization_details` Rich Authorization Requests
(RAR) claim.

1. Click **Applications**.

1. Click **STS clients**.

1. Click **Add STS client**.

1. Configure the general, authentication, token, proof-of-possession, and
   endpoint settings.

   <Tabs>

   <Tab heading="Authentication">

   1. Leave the client authentication method at **Default**.

   1. Click **Next**.

   </Tab>
   <Tab heading="Token exchange">

   1. Click **Subject token** dropdown and check **Access token**.

   1. Click **Actor token** dropdown and check **Access token**.

   1. Click **Requested token** dropdown and check **Access token**.

   ![Token exchange settings](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-verify-app13.png)

   1. Leave other token exchange settings as-is.

   1. Click **Next**.

   </Tab>
   <Tab heading="Requested token">

   1. Click the **Access token format** dropdown.
   1. Select **JWT**
   1. Leave all other values at their default settings.
   1. Click **Next**.

   </Tab>
   <Tab heading="Proof-of-possession">

   Unless you need to change them, you can accept all proof-of-possession settings
   defaults, and click **Next**.

   </Tab>
   <Tab heading="Endpoint">

   At a minimum, you need to configure the **Introspect mapping** value in the
   endpoint configuration.

   1. Under **Introspect mapping** click the **Add attribute** dropdown.

      ![Endpoint configuration](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-verify-app14.png)

   1. Click **Add custom rule**.

   1. In the **Request rule** text area, enter this custom rule:

      ```json
      {"sub":requestContext["actor_token"].sub}
      ```

   1. In the **Target attribute** field, enter `actor-token`.

   1. Click **OK**.

   </Tab>
   </Tabs>

1. Define your custom scopes and API access:

    1. Unless you need to relax any settings, you can leave everything except for
      **Authorization detail types** unchanged.

    1. For **Authorization detail types**, select **vault:path_access**.

    1. Check the box for all the user permissions your use case requires.

    1. Click **Next**.

1. Click **Complete setup**. You do not need to apply an access policy.


## Step 8: Validate token retrieval

Use your application client ID and client secret values with the `oauth2c` tool
to get a token from Verify as a validation step.

1. Get your application details:

    1. Click **Applications** > **Applications**.

    1. Click the gear icon next to your application name to open settings.

    1. Click **Sign-on**.

    1. Scroll down to **Client ID** and copy the value; paste the value somewhere
      safe to use later.

    1. Click the copy to clipboard icon next to **Client secret** and then paste
      the value somewhere safe to use later.

1. Open a new terminal.

1. Export your Verify tenant name, client ID, and secret as environment variables:

    ```shell-session
    $ export IBM_VERIFY_TENANT=`<tenant name>`                          \
        IBM_VERIFY_CLIENT_ID=`<client ID generated from previous step>` \
        IBM_VERIFY_CLIENT_SECRET=`<client secret generated from previous step>`
    ```

1. Request an example token with the oauth2c command-line tool.

    ```shell-session
    $ oauth2c https://"${IBM_VERIFY_TENANT}".verify.ibm.com/oauth2 \
        --pkce                                                     \
        --client-id "${IBM_VERIFY_CLIENT_ID}"                      \
        --client-secret "${IBM_VERIFY_CLIENT_SECRET}"              \
        --response-types code                                      \
        --response-mode query                                      \
        --grant-type authorization_code                            \
        --auth-method client_secret_basic --no-browser
    ```

1. Note the URL under `Go to the following URL:` in the output. Visit that
   URL in a browser to complete the authentication flow. The workflow then
   outputs more indicators of success.

   <CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

   ```plaintext
   ...snip...
    SUCCESS  Obtained authorization code
   ...snip...
   SUCCESS  Exchanged authorization code for access token
   ```

   </CodeBlockConfig>

The final output string after the SUCCESS messages represents the JWT value,
which validates both the workflow and token issuance from Verify.


## Step 9: Validate token exchange

You can also exchange the AI agent (actor) and human user (subject) tokens with
RAR `authorization_detail` claims with a similar workflow by providing token
values from tokens issued for both the AI agent and the human.

1. Export the AI agent token value as the AGENT_TOKEN environment variable.

    ```shell-session
    $ export AGENT_TOKEN=...
    ```

1. Export the human user token value as the HUMAN_TOKEN environment variable.

    ```shell-session
    $ export HUMAN_TOKEN=...
    ```

1. Export the DELEGATION_TOKEN environment variable to hold the output of
   the token exchange.

    ```shell-session
    $ export DELEGATION_TOKEN=$(curl --request POST \
    --url https://vv-agentic-iam-demo.ite4.idng.ibmcloudsecurity.com/oauth2/token \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
    --data grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange \
    --data subject_token="${HUMAN_TOKEN}" \
    --data subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token \
    --data actor_token="${AGENT_TOKEN}" \
    --data actor_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token \
    --data client_id="${IBM_VERIFY_CLIENT_ID}" \
    --data client_secret="${IBM_VERIFY_CLIENT_SECRET}" \
    --data 'authorization_details=[{"type":"vault:path_access","path":"secret-v2/data/shared-secret/foo", "capabilities":["create"]}]' | jq -r '.access_token)
    ```


## Step 10: Save your provider information

Confirm your subject and actor details from Verify. To configure agentic IAM,
you must have the following information:

Value                   | Environmental variable  | Description
----------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------
Delegated JWT           | `DELEGATED_JWT`         | The OBO with authorization details JWT as obtained after token exchange via the STS client.
Issuer URL              | `ISSUER`                | URL identifying the authentication entry point app itself
Human (subject) user ID | `SUBJECT_EXT_ID`        | User ID of the **subject** user from your IdP application
AI (actor) user ID      | `ACTOR_EXT_ID`          | User ID of the **actor** user from your IdP application
Key endpoint            | `JWKS_URI`              | URL where clients can download public keys (JWKS) from your Verify instance


We recommend setting the following environment variables to make Vault
configuration more convenient:

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```shell-session
$ export                                 \
    VAULT_ADDR="<your_vault_server_url>" \
    VAULT_TOKEN="<token_string>"         \
    DELEGATED_JWT="<idp-issued-jwt>"     \
    SUBJECT_EXT_ID="<human_user_id>"     \
    ACTOR_EXT_ID="<ai_user_id>"          \
    JWKS_URI="<jwks_uri>"                \
    ISSUER="<issuer_uid>"
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

For example:

```shell-session
$ export                                                        \
    VAULT_ADDR="http://127.0.0.1:8200"                          \
    VAULT_TOKEN="hvs.000000000000000000000000"                  \
    DELEGATED_JWT="000000...000000...signature_bytes_here..."   \
    SUBJECT_EXT_ID="0000000000"                                 \
    ACTOR_EXT_ID="0000000000"                                   \
    JWKS_URI="mydomain.verify.ibm.com/oauth2/jwks"              \
    ISSUER="mydomain.verify.ibm.com/oauth2"
```
